newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat up in nearby contracts on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat up in nearby contracts on tight supply.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose further on Thursday in near-term contracts but fell away in more distant contracts.
In a reasonably active day when 15 lots were traded, May 1997 gained A$1.50 a tonne to A$191.00 while July 1997 added A$2.50 to A$193.00 on the trade. January 1998 traded down A$2.50 to A$188.00.
Settlement prices in more distant contracts fell by up to A$7.50 a tonne for November 1997 with most declines in the A$2.00-A$3.00 range.
Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said the market reflected difficult near-term feed grain supply and high demand.
Farmers, expecting the grain market to rise further, were reluctant sellers, he said.
"The grain buyers are well aware that they will have to coax this grain out of some of these guys and the only way to coax is to lift the price," he said.
